How to choose between them

Camphorous oils vary in harshness

Eucalyptus is the sharpest, tea tree the most medicinal, niaouli and ravensara noticeably softer. If eucalyptus feels too strong, start with niaouli.

Warm spices need the lowest dilutions

Clove bud and cinnamon leaf are sensitisers with ceilings of 0.5 and 0.6 per cent. These are not beginner oils, and sensitisation does not wear off.

Fennel carries the longest warning list

Avoid in pregnancy and breastfeeding, with oestrogen-sensitive conditions, and around children. If any of that applies, coriander seed gives similar warmth without the restrictions.

How people use these

◌

Steam inhalation

Three drops in a bowl of hot water, a towel over the head, a few minutes of breathing. Three — not ten.

✋

Diffuse seasonally

Four drops of eucalyptus with lemon and tea tree is the standard winter blend.

♨

Surface sprays

Tea tree, thyme and lemon in a spray bottle, where their strength is an advantage rather than a hazard.

Questions about immunity oils

Do these oils treat colds or boost immunity?

No, and we are not going to suggest otherwise. They smell clearing, and many people find steam comforting when congested — but the steam is doing most of that work, and neither will shorten an illness. Essential oils are not medicine.

Why do you call it the immunity collection then?

Because it is what people come looking for, and pretending otherwise would just make the range harder to navigate. The name describes the shelf, not a claim about the contents.

Are these safe around children?

Largely not. Eucalyptus, niaouli and ravensara are high in 1,8-cineole, which can affect breathing in babies and young children. Clove, cinnamon and thyme should be kept away from children entirely. Ask a doctor before diffusing any of these in a house with a small child.

Which are safe around cats and dogs?

Tea tree is genuinely toxic to cats and dogs, including as vapour in a closed room. As a general rule we would not diffuse anything from this collection around pets without veterinary advice.
